definitions.explanation: Damage, irritation, or wear caused by repeated rubbing or friction on a surface. Applies to skin (chafing), fabric (wear), or other materials.

examples.english: I got a blister from my shoes rubbing.

examples.japanese: {襟|えり}の{擦|す}れが{目立|めだ}つようになった。
examples.english: The wear on the collar has become noticeable.

examples.japanese: {長距離|ちょうきょり}を{走|はし}ると、{太|ふと}ももの{内側|うちがわ}に{擦|す}れが{起|お}きやすい。
examples.english: When running long distances, chafing tends to occur on the inner thighs.

notes:
The noun form of {擦|す}れる (to rub, to chafe). Frequently appears in compounds and is an everyday word for physical wear caused by friction. The reading changes to ずれ in some compounds (e.g., {靴|くつ}ずれ).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {靴|くつ}{擦|ず}れ: shoe blister, shoe rubbing
- {擦|す}れ{傷|きず}: abrasion, scrape wound
- {擦|す}れて{痛|いた}い: hurts from rubbing
- {股|また}{擦|ず}れ: inner thigh chafing
- {袖|そで}の{擦|す}れ: wear on sleeves

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {摩擦|まさつ}: friction — the physical force itself, more technical and scientific
- {傷|きず}: wound, scratch — broader term for any damage or injury
- {磨耗|まもう}: wear, abrasion — more technical, used for mechanical or material wear
